I don't know about you guys but it seems to me pretty much everyone has something they don't like about driving (especially other drivers). What do you think about making the test harder/more "behind the wheel" training/more something? How would you change it? Do you not think this is the case?
Are you for or against a more involved license process?

I don't think that the main problem is the practical aspect of driving, but the theoretical aspect. There are far more violators of traffic regulation, than there are people who just can't handle a car.

Moreover, there are two kinds of traffic regulation violators: the kind that purposefully violates traffic regulations and the kind that unknowingly violates traffic regulations. The amount of people associated with the former kind only decreases if there is more supervision on the road by e.g. police officers and correct consequences are imposed. The latter kind can be corrected by educating these drivers, and here we use the license process to make sure everybody has had a certain level of education. I think that one theoretical exam, when you apply for a license, is not enough. In my opinion it would be better to let new drivers retake this exam a few times in the first few years of their driving career. This way, traffic rules will become better known among the population.

EDIT: I only have experience with the license process of most European countries. I have no idea if this is similar in the rest of the world.

I think it should be like this:

  • Permit test first. This is a free paper test given by the local DMV. It should be 100 questions or more, and not timed.

  • Driving test. This proves you know how to turn it on, make it move, and turn it back off without murdering a school bus. 5 such tests, each more difficult than the last, but none contain anything that isn't required somewhere on a public road every day.

  • Permit granted. This costs $50 and allows you to drive for 1 year. Any at-fault accidents the whole process starts over. A GPS device reports your speed, braking, acceleration, corner speed, etc. You get two whole shots at this.

  • Monthly retesting and evaluation. 1 day per month during your permit period, you must take an abridged and randomized version of the original test, and a refresher test course.

  • License. After your one year you have the option of purchasing your license IF you AND your instructor feel that you are competent enough. If either of you feel that you aren't ready, you will be given a further 6 months on your permit. Once you have your license, the GPS is removed, and you purchase your license for $600.

  • Penalties. Moving violations would remain largely the same. You are allowed 1 at fault accidents involving 2 or more vehicles per 5 year span. If the accident requires repairs to another vehicle besides your own that your insurance must cover, this counts. Anything involving your vehicle that causes your license to be suspended will result in starting the entire process over (testing, permit for a year, $600 license, etc).

  • Insurance agencies are required to give a bonus/incentive to those who opt to keep their permit and GPS for the extra 6 months, and for those who don't have accidents.

  • DWIs have 2 chances. First offense, your license is revoked for 2 years, whole process is different when you reapply however - classes every weekend for several months, permit is 2 years, license is $4000. Second offense is permanent revocation with potential for reevaluation after 8 years, permit is 2 years, license is $8,000. Third offense is permanent revocation with no chance for reevaluation or relicensing, felony to ever drive a vehicle again.

Laws vary, but generally -- candidates have to return or donate unused contribution UNLESS they plan to run for office again.

However, "running for another office" is quite liberally interpreted, and politicians often hold onto, and spend campaign funds decades after their last campaign. They officially aren't allowed to make personal purchases -- but can spend it on their offices, meetings, and ongoing activities.
